# Pattern Review: Brackenford Hall

## Input Quality and Limitations

The log covers three distinct events in one month, with one occurrence per event. E1 and E2 have supported diagnoses: technicians reproduced each fault, confirmed a damaged cable, and found that replacement removed the fault. E3 has no investigation or diagnosis, so its cause is unknown.

## Summary

| Candidate | Occurrences | Distinct Instances | Cause Consistency | Confidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Damaged cable causing projector failure: E1, E2 | 2 | 2 | Same independently confirmed cause | High for recurrence within this log |
| Display interruption: E1, E2, E3 | 3 | 3 | Two confirmed cable faults; one unknown | High for recurring symptoms, insufficient evidence for one shared cause |

## Genuine Patterns

Damaged cables caused projector failures in E1 and E2, across different events and rooms. Reproduction and successful cable replacement support the same cause in both instances.

No contradictory diagnosis is recorded for this pair. However, two instances do not establish a venue-wide problem, explain why the cables were damaged, or establish E3’s cause.

## Misleading Surface Patterns

None is confirmed: the log does not demonstrate similar wording arising from different diagnosed causes.

Nevertheless, grouping E3’s “screen goes black” with E1 and E2 as another cable fault would be unsupported. Similar symptoms do not establish the same cause.

## Isolated Signals, Not Yet Patterns

E3 is one undiagnosed instance. It supports the broader observation of display interruption, but not a separate causal pattern or an additional confirmed cable failure.

## Suggested Actions for Human Approval

- Investigate E3 before assigning it to a causal group.
- Have a person check the E1 and E2 diagnoses and consider whether a targeted cable inspection is warranted. No wider replacement or process change is established by this review.

## What This Sample Cannot Tell You

This complete three-event monthly log establishes two confirmed cable-fault instances, not a long-term failure rate, future risk, or venue-wide root cause. It cannot show whether E3 shares that cause or whether cable damage has a common underlying driver.
